boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain State University of New York at Cortland
boards.description: Ten currently listed, under-21-safe Cortland destinations with evening availability. Check the source before leaving, as hours can change.

cards.title: Kalash Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 54 Main St, Cortland
cards.notes: Use the posted daily midnight closing time for a late Main Street food stop; confirm availability or ordering details directly before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Main Street restaurant with daily hours listed through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalash Kitchen lists Cortland hours ending at 12 a.m. every day and gives its address as 54 Main St.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Monday–Wednesday 10 a.m.–12 a.m. and Thursday–Sunday 11 a.m.–12 a.m.

cards.title: BRIX
cards.subtitle: 60 Main St, Cortland
cards.notes: On Friday or Saturday, plan around the posted 11 p.m. close and use BRIX’s official site for current menu, takeout, or reservation information.
cards.short_summary: Main Street restaurant with Friday–Saturday hours to 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: BRIX lists its address as 60 Main St and Friday–Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Friday–Saturday hours until 11 p.m.; other listed days close at 9 p.m.

cards.title: Pontillo's Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 124 Groton Ave, Cortland
cards.notes: For a late pickup or delivery plan, use the restaurant’s official ordering link and allow for the posted ready-time estimates before closing.
cards.short_summary: Pizza restaurant listing daily service until 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pontillo's official site lists 124 Groton Ave and says it is open daily from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site states “OPEN DAILY 11 AM -10 PM” and provides pickup and delivery ordering.

cards.title: Pudgie's Pizza Cortland
cards.subtitle: 75 N Main St, Cortland
cards.notes: Make this a Friday or Saturday option when the official listing extends to 10 p.m.; verify whether delivery is still accepting orders.
cards.short_summary: North Main pizza shop with Friday–Saturday service to 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pudgie's Pizza Cortland lists Friday–Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–10 p.m. and delivery until 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Sunday–Thursday until 9 p.m. and Friday–Saturday, including delivery, until 10 p.m.

cards.title: Arctic Bites
cards.subtitle: 178 Clinton Ave, Cortland
cards.notes: Use the Friday–Saturday 11 p.m. closing window for an evening dessert or food stop, then check the official page for any update.
cards.short_summary: Clinton Avenue restaurant with Friday–Saturday hours to 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Arctic Bites lists 178 Clinton Ave and Friday–Saturday hours from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Monday–Thursday until 10 p.m., Friday–Saturday until 11 p.m., and Sunday until 10 p.m.

cards.title: KFC on State Route 281
cards.subtitle: 3890 State Route 281, Cortland
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location page to confirm drive-thru or dining details, with posted daily restaurant hours extending through 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: Route 281 quick-service restaurant listed open to 11 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: KFC's official Cortland location page lists 3890 State Route 281 and 10 a.m.–11 p.m. hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists restaurant hours of 10 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Moe's Southwest Grill
cards.subtitle: 872 Route 13, Cortland
cards.notes: For an evening Route 13 food stop, check the official location page and place an order before its listed 10 p.m. daily close.
cards.short_summary: Route 13 restaurant with daily hours listed through 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Moe's official Cortland location page lists 872 Route 13 and hours of 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Denny's on River Street
cards.subtitle: 1 River St, Cortland
cards.notes: Schedule this option for Friday or Saturday, when the official location page lists 10 p.m. closing; check that day’s listing before travel.
cards.short_summary: River Street diner with Friday–Saturday hours listed to 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's official Cortland location page lists Friday and Saturday restaurant hours from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday–Saturday until 10 p.m.; Monday–Thursday and Sunday until 9 p.m.

cards.title: 281 Bowl
cards.subtitle: 3898 State Route 281, Cortland
cards.notes: For a non-dining evening outing, call before leaving because open-bowling availability can change with leagues, parties, and tournaments.
cards.short_summary: Bowling destination listing Friday and Saturday operation until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: 281 Bowl lists Friday and Saturday hours until 12 a.m. and advises visitors to call ahead for open-bowling availability.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday 3 p.m.–12 a.m. and Saturday 1 p.m.–12 a.m.; it says hours and lanes can vary, so call ahead.

cards.title: SUNY Cortland Dining Services
cards.subtitle: SUNY Cortland campus
cards.notes: Consult the Auxiliary Services hours page before going; it states campus residential and retail dining options can run as late as 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: Campus dining system with stated operating range up to 11 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland Auxiliary Services states its campus residential and retail dining options have hours ranging from 7:30 a.m. to 11 p.m., seven days a week.
cards.source_title: SUNY Cortland Auxiliary Services Dining Services
cards.access_notes: Official dining page states hours range from 7:30 a.m. to 11 p.m., seven days a week; consult its hours-of-operation link for venue-specific service.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus places that support studying, recreation, programs, or cultural activity.

cards.title: Corey Union
cards.subtitle: Campus activities, meeting rooms, study areas and services
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical meet-up point: check the campus calendar, visit a student organization, or settle into one of its study areas.
cards.short_summary: A student-services hub with space for meetings, programs, studying and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says Corey Union houses meeting rooms, offices, study areas, dining, student clubs and the Student Government Association.
cards.source_title: Campus Activities and Corey Union | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Building services and room use may vary by event or office.

cards.title: Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Research help, technology and individual or group study
cards.notes: Choose a workspace that fits your task, then use the Research Help Desk or online librarian chat when you need help finding sources.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines research support with study rooms, carrels and shared seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Library offers group study rooms, study carrels, the Bookmark Cafe and other spaces, and provides research help to the SUNY Cortland community.
cards.access_notes: Library spaces have differing noise expectations; consult the library map and policies.

cards.title: Bookmark Cafe
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library’s first-floor cafe entrance and study area
cards.notes: Enter from Prospect Terrace for a study-area route into the library, and use it as a starting point before heading to a quieter floor.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor library area that connects the cafe entrance with study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s library map says the Bookmark Cafe entrance leads to a study area and the Advisement and Transition Office.
cards.access_notes: The Bookmark Cafe entrance does not have a push-to-enter option, according to the library accessibility map.

cards.title: Memorial Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a project idea and confirm available equipment or support before visiting; the Makerspace sits among second-floor open seating and computing resources.
cards.short_summary: A named making area integrated into the library’s collaborative second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s library map lists the Makerspace on Memorial Library’s second floor alongside open seating study areas and the Computer Applications Lab.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: The second floor permits noise and is typically a moderate-noise area.

cards.title: Teaching Materials Center
cards.subtitle: First floor of Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use this named library destination when your coursework calls for teaching resources, then pair the visit with nearby first-floor open seating or research help.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library center for teaching materials within a larger study and support zone.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists the Teaching Materials Center among Memorial Library’s spaces and places it on the first floor in its map description.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: The first floor allows noise in most areas.

cards.title: Student Life Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation, social spaces and a dining hall near campus center
cards.notes: Plan an active break around the facility you need, such as the track, climbing wall, gymnasium, pool or fitness areas, and follow recreation rules.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose recreation building with fitness features, social space and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says the Student Life Center includes a pool, gymnasium, running track, weight room, climbing wall, group exercise room and social spaces.
cards.access_notes: Recreation access and program availability may be subject to campus recreation policies.

cards.title: Holsten Pool
cards.subtitle: Park Center aquatic facility
cards.notes: Check campus recreation availability before going, then use the Park Center layout to locate the first-floor locker rooms and second-floor spectator access.
cards.short_summary: A named Park Center pool with dedicated spectator and locker-room locations.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies Holsten Pool in Park Center, with locker rooms on the first floor and spectator seating accessed from the second floor.
cards.access_notes: Availability for swimming or spectating depends on the facility schedule and event use.

cards.title: Dowd Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor of Dowd Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Look for the current exhibition before your visit, then enter Dowd Fine Arts Center from the most convenient building entrance to reach the gallery.
cards.short_summary: A campus exhibition space housed in Dowd Fine Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says Dowd Gallery is on the first floor of Dowd Fine Arts Center and can be accessed from any entrance to the building.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition access may depend on the gallery’s current schedule.

cards.title: Brooks Museum
cards.subtitle: Moffett Center, Room 2126
cards.notes: Pair a museum stop with nearby campus buildings, and use the room location in Moffett Center to find the collection before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named campus museum located in Moffett Center.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies Brooks Museum as a museum venue in Moffett Center, Room 2126.
cards.access_notes: Confirm museum access or scheduled programming before visiting.

cards.title: Park Center Alumni Arena
cards.subtitle: First-floor Park Center athletic and event venue
cards.notes: Check the university events calendar or athletics schedule before going, and use the surrounding Park Center lots only in accordance with posted parking rules.
cards.short_summary: A large Park Center venue used for athletics as well as performances and events.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists Park Center Alumni Arena as both an athletic facility and a performance and event space on Park Center’s first floor.
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on the scheduled event and its admission or attendance requirements.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost places and activities on campus or in the Cortland area.

cards.title: Explore Bowers Science Museum
cards.subtitle: Bowers Hall, SUNY Cortland
cards.notes: Walk through the lobby exhibits on fossils, rocks, chemistry and physics, then spend time with the digital planetarium displays.
cards.short_summary: A campus science museum with natural-history and interactive exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland states that Bowers Science Museum is open to the public and free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty and campus visitors; confirm current building access before visiting.

cards.title: See an exhibition at Dowd Gallery
cards.subtitle: Dowd Fine Arts Center, SUNY Cortland
cards.notes: Drop into the gallery to view the current exhibition, or attend an accompanying artist talk, lecture, performance or workshop.
cards.short_summary: Campus gallery presentations and related programs are publicly accessible.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says all Dowd Gallery exhibitions and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Walk-ins are welcome; the gallery is closed when the university is not in session.

cards.title: Browse Memorial Library’s print collections
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library, SUNY Cortland
cards.notes: Meet up for a quiet browse of the print collections or settle into a reading session with materials available on the premises.
cards.short_summary: A campus library option that welcomes the general public for on-site print resources.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s borrowing policy says Memorial Library is open to the general public and that print resources are accessible to all on the premises.
cards.access_notes: On-site print-resource access is public; electronic databases and computer labs have separate eligibility rules.

cards.entity_name: Use WiFi at Cortland Free Library
cards.title: Connect at Cortland Free Library
cards.subtitle: Cortland Free Library, 32 Church Street
cards.notes: Bring a device and use the LibraryPublic network in the building or on the library grounds for a low-key shared work session.
cards.short_summary: Password-free library WiFi available around the building and grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland Free Library states that WiFi is available 24/7 in the building and on library grounds, with no password needed.
cards.access_notes: Observe the library’s Internet and Computer Use Policy while connected.

cards.title: Borrow a book, movie or game
cards.subtitle: Cortland Free Library, 32 Church Street
cards.notes: If you live in the Finger Lakes Library System region, bring identification and address proof to get a card and borrow together.
cards.short_summary: Eligible regional residents can borrow physical and digital materials at no charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland Free Library says eligible Finger Lakes Library System residents may get a card for free and use it to borrow books, music, movies and more for free.
cards.access_notes: Free-card eligibility requires regional residence plus proof of ID and address; temporary residents have a separate card process.

cards.title: Take a free swim at Yaman Beach
cards.subtitle: Yaman Park, Cortland
cards.notes: Plan a daytime summer swim and bring what you need for the beach; use the posted seasonal operating window as your guide.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed free swimming facility at Yaman Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cortland lists Yaman Beach among its free swimming facilities.
cards.access_notes: The city lists Yaman Beach hours as 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.; verify seasonal availability before going.

cards.entity_name: Swim at C. C. Wickwire Pool
cards.title: Swim at C. C. Wickwire Pool
cards.subtitle: Suggett Park, Cortland
cards.notes: Gather a friend for an afternoon pool session at Suggett Park and check the city schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed free swimming facility in Suggett Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cortland lists C. C. Wickwire Pool at Suggett Park as a free swimming facility.
cards.access_notes: The city lists Wickwire Pool hours as noon to 7 p.m.; verify seasonal availability before going.

cards.entity_name: Walk the trails at Lime Hollow Nature Center
cards.title: Walk Lime Hollow’s trails
cards.subtitle: Lime Hollow Nature Center, 338 McLean Road
cards.notes: Choose an easy, moderate or difficult route, download or pick up a trail map, and make the outing fit your group’s pace.
cards.short_summary: No-charge trails with multiple difficulty options near Cortland.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland County’s activity guide lists Lime Hollow Nature Center trails as having no charge.
cards.access_notes: The county guide notes that trail maps are available online or at the nature center.

cards.entity_name: Walk the East End Community Center indoor track
cards.title: Walk the East End indoor track
cards.subtitle: East End Community Center, 46 Elm Street
cards.notes: Use the indoor track for a casual walking lap with a friend, signing in at the center before you start.
cards.short_summary: A no-charge indoor walking option in Cortland.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland County’s activity guide lists the East End Community Center indoor track as no charge.
cards.access_notes: The county guide lists access Monday through Friday, 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., with sign-in at the center.

cards.title: Walk the Bennett Street Field trails
cards.subtitle: Bennett Street Field, McGraw
cards.notes: Head to the trails around the soccer field for an easy nearby walk, keeping the route social and at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: No-charge walking trails around McGraw’s soccer field.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland County’s activity guide lists walking trails around the soccer field at Bennett Street Field as no charge.
cards.access_notes: Listed at Bennett Street Field on Elm Street Extension in McGraw.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Memorial Library study environments, ranging from collaborative seating to designated quiet and reservable spaces.

cards.entity_name: Memorial Library First-Floor Open Seating Study Areas
cards.title: First-Floor Open Seating
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · noise permitted
cards.notes: Set up in the first-floor open seating areas when conversation and active campus movement will not disrupt your work.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor option for work that can tolerate ambient noise.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists open seating study areas on Memorial Library’s first floor and states that noise is allowed in most first-floor areas.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Located in Memorial Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Memorial Library Second-Floor Open Seating Study Areas
cards.title: Second-Floor Open Seating
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · moderate-noise floor
cards.notes: Use the second-floor open seating areas for reading, laptop work, or short work sessions in a moderate-noise setting.
cards.short_summary: Open seating on a floor designated as typically moderate noise.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists open seating study areas on Memorial Library’s second floor and describes that floor as typically a moderate-noise area.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Located in Memorial Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Memorial Library Third-Floor Wing A Open Seating Study Areas
cards.title: Third-Floor Wing A Seating
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · low-noise floor
cards.notes: Head to third-floor Wing A when you want open seating in a lower-noise library environment for sustained individual work.
cards.short_summary: Open seating on Memorial Library’s low-noise third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists open seating study areas in Memorial Library’s third-floor Wing A and describes the third floor as typically low noise.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Located in Memorial Library, third-floor Wing A; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Quiet Area
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · Wing A
cards.notes: Choose the fourth-floor quiet area for focused reading or writing, and keep conversations and calls for another library zone.
cards.short_summary: The library’s specifically designated quiet floor area.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies Memorial Library’s fourth-floor Wing A as a quiet area.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Fourth-floor Wing A of Memorial Library; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · individual rooms
cards.notes: Look for an individual room when you need a contained workspace; these fourth-floor rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: Individual study rooms in the library’s designated quiet area.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Library reports 34 fourth-floor study rooms; they are for individual study, first-come first-served, and require neither reservation nor key for SUNY Cortland students, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: 4th Floor Study Rooms | SUNY Cortland Library
cards.access_notes: Available first-come, first-served to SUNY Cortland students, staff, and faculty; no reservation or key is required.

cards.title: Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · reservation and key checkout
cards.notes: Reserve a group room ahead, then use the key checkout process when your project needs a dedicated shared workspace.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms for pairs and larger study groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Library has three group study rooms for two people and six for groups of four or more; current students reserve them and sign out a key.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Group Study Room | SUNY Cortland Library
cards.access_notes: Available for checkout to current students; a reservation and key checkout are required.

cards.title: Bookmark Cafe Study Area
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use the study area reached from the Bookmark Cafe entrance when you want a first-floor library setup near the café.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor study area adjacent to the Bookmark Cafe entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s library map states that the Bookmark Cafe entrance leads to a study area; the cafe is on the library’s first floor.
cards.access_notes: Enter through Memorial Library’s Bookmark Cafe entrance; consult current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Computer Applications Lab
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · second floor
cards.notes: Bring work that benefits from a computer-lab setting and confirm whether the room is open rather than assigned to instruction.
cards.short_summary: A named computer-lab resource on Memorial Library’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists the Computer Applications Lab on the second floor of Memorial Library.
cards.source_title: Library Map Text Descriptions | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Located on Memorial Library’s second floor; verify availability and current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Phylis Duke Fralick ’58 and Fredric Fralick ’59 Teaching Materials Center
cards.title: Teaching Materials Center
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use the Teaching Materials Center when course work calls for teacher-education collections, materials, or a library-based worktable.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor center with curriculum-focused collections and services.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies the Teaching Materials Center on Memorial Library’s first floor and says it provides collections, instruction, outreach, and research services for teacher education students and faculty.
cards.access_notes: Located on Memorial Library’s first floor; its services are described for SUNY Cortland teacher education students and faculty.

cards.title: Inspiration Station
cards.subtitle: Teaching Materials Center · Memorial Library
cards.notes: Plan a small-group working session in Inspiration Station when you need a separate room for collaborative academic preparation.
cards.short_summary: A separate small-group collaboration room within the Teaching Materials Center.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland describes Inspiration Station as a separate room for small-group collaborations, located downstairs in the Teaching Materials Center.
cards.source_title: Library offers crafting space for recreation and education | SUNY Cortland
cards.access_notes: Located in the Teaching Materials Center in Memorial Library; confirm access arrangements with the library before planning a session.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown and near-campus destinations, each tied to its surrounding corridor.

cards.title: Cortland Free Library
cards.subtitle: Church Street corridor, one block west of Main Street
cards.notes: Enter from the Court Street side for elevator access, then use the public reading areas or borrow materials during posted library hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library stop on the Church and Court streets block.
cards.evidence_claim: The library is located at 32 Church Street; its site lists public hours and identifies the Court Street entrance for elevator accessibility.
cards.source_title: Location, Hours & Contact – Cortland Free Library
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours before going; the site notes that weather closings can affect service.

cards.title: Cortland City Farmers Market
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, in front of City Hall
cards.notes: Plan this stop for a listed Tuesday or Saturday market day and browse the vendors in front of City Hall at Court and Church streets.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled downtown market on the Court Street civic block.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Cortland places the market at 25 Court Street, in front of City Hall at the corner of Court and Church, and lists Tuesday and Saturday market times.
cards.access_notes: The listing gives Tuesdays and Saturdays, 8 a.m.–2 p.m.; confirm that the market is operating before making the trip.

cards.title: City of Cortland City Hall
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, beside Fire Headquarters
cards.notes: Use this civic-block landmark as an orientation point, and check the city calendar or department pages before visiting for a specific public-service need.
cards.short_summary: The city-government anchor at 25 Court Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Cortland lists its contact address as 25 Court Street, Cortland, NY 13045.
cards.access_notes: This is an active government building; consult the relevant city department for visitor procedures or meeting details.

cards.title: Cortland Fire Headquarters
cards.subtitle: Court Street corridor, next to City Hall
cards.notes: View the historic exterior from the public street and keep driveways and apparatus access clear; use the department site for public programs or contact details.
cards.short_summary: A 1914 firehouse on the Court Street civic block.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland Fire Department identifies its headquarters at 21 Court Street as a historic building constructed in 1914.
cards.access_notes: This is an operating emergency-services facility; observe from public areas and do not obstruct vehicles or entrances.

cards.title: Cortland County Courthouse
cards.subtitle: Greenbush Street corridor, off West Court Street
cards.notes: Use the public frontage as a Greenbush Street landmark; if entering for court business, review the court’s accessibility and building information first.
cards.short_summary: A county-court destination on the Greenbush Street block.
cards.evidence_claim: New York Courts lists the Cortland County Courthouse at 46 Greenbush Street and describes elevators, public parking, restrooms, and an ADA-accessible entrance.
cards.source_title: CORTLAND COUNTY - Courthouse | New York Courts
cards.access_notes: Court access and security procedures can vary; confirm the relevant court office’s requirements before entering.

cards.title: Suggett House Museum
cards.subtitle: Homer Avenue corridor, near the downtown civic blocks
cards.notes: Check the museum’s exhibit schedule, then join a guided tour to see county-history artifacts in the former Suggett family home.
cards.short_summary: A local-history museum housed in the Suggett family home.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Historical Society states that the Suggett House Museum holds its artifacts and tells Cortland County history through exhibits; it lists guided tours Wednesday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Suggett House | Cortland County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The Historical Society lists guided tours Wednesday–Saturday, 12–5 p.m.; verify exhibit and tour availability before going.

cards.title: All My Friends Books
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Browse new and used books, stationery, and bookish gifts, or check the shop calendar for an in-store event before heading to 51 Main Street.
cards.short_summary: An all-ages independent bookstore on Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: All My Friends Books identifies its Cortland shop at 51 Main Street and describes it as a general-interest, all-ages independent bookstore with new and used books.
cards.source_title: All My Friends Books | Indie Bookstores in Cortland & Skaneateles, NY
cards.access_notes: The shop lists daily hours on its website; check for updates and event-specific timing before visiting.

cards.title: The Local Food Market & Cafe
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Use this Main Street stop for a market-and-cafe visit, and check the business directly for its current menu, service details, and availability.
cards.short_summary: A named food-market and cafe destination on North Main.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Convention & Visitors Bureau lists The Local Food Market at 37 Main Street in Cortland.
cards.source_title: The Port Watson Mini-Conference Center | Experience Cortland
cards.access_notes: Confirm current hours and offerings with the business before visiting.

cards.title: Lot 1 Vintage
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor, downtown Cortland
cards.notes: Add this storefront to a Main Street walk if you want to browse vintage goods; verify current opening information with the shop before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A named vintage storefront on the Main Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025 Cortland Travel Guide lists Lot 1 Vintage at 79 Main Street, Cortland, with its website.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the shop’s current hours and access arrangements directly before visiting.

cards.title: Squires Block Clock Tower
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at Port Watson Street
cards.notes: Pause at the Main and Port Watson streets corner to photograph the clock-tower building, then use the historical society account to trace the site’s earlier uses.
cards.short_summary: A documented clock-tower landmark at a downtown Main Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cortland County Historical Society states that the Squires Block, with its iconic clock tower, replaced the Eagle Store at the Main and Port Watson streets corner in 1883.
cards.source_title: Main Street – City of Cortland | Cortland County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: View and photograph the exterior from public sidewalks while observing traffic conditions at the Main and Port Watson streets corner.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented SUNY Cortland rituals, annual observances and ceremonial objects that mark campus life.

cards.title: Follow the Cortaca Jug
cards.subtitle: Annual Cortland–Ithaca football rivalry trophy
cards.notes: See the painted traveling jug and check the rivalry’s official history before game week; each year’s score is added to the trophy.
cards.short_summary: A ceramic milk jug has traveled between Cortland and Ithaca since 1959.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says the Cortaca Jug was first awarded in 1959 as a traveling trophy, and the score is added to it every year.
cards.access_notes: Game and related-event details vary by year; consult the official Cortaca page before attending.

cards.title: Start with Academic Convocation
cards.subtitle: Opening-of-year academic ceremony
cards.notes: If you are eligible to attend, watch the faculty procession and formal welcome; the revived ceremony marks the start of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: Cortland revived this opening academic tradition in 2003.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland describes Academic Convocation as a tradition revived in 2003 that marks the beginning of students’ academic journeys.
cards.access_notes: Participation and venue information are announced for each academic year.

cards.title: Recognize the Kente Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Multicultural graduation-stole celebration
cards.notes: Learn what the woven kente stole represents and attend respectfully when invited; the Cortland ceremony honors graduating seniors’ achievements.
cards.short_summary: A Cortland ceremony introduced in 1994 recognizes graduating seniors with kente stoles.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland reports that its Kente Ceremony began in 1994 and encourages graduating seniors to participate with family and campus friends.
cards.access_notes: This is a formal graduation-related ceremony; participation details are set by its organizers.

cards.title: Join The Big Event
cards.subtitle: Annual student volunteer day
cards.notes: Sign up through the event organizers when dates are posted and be ready for a local service assignment with other Cortland students.
cards.short_summary: Students gather annually for organized volunteer work in the Cortland community.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies The Big Event as an annual event matching hundreds of students with local volunteer opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Volunteer assignments, registration and timing are announced by the university for each event.

cards.title: Present at Transformations
cards.subtitle: Annual student research and creativity conference
cards.notes: Browse the program or present your work when eligible; the day centers student and campus scholarship through talks and poster sessions.
cards.short_summary: Transformations is Cortland’s annual forum for research and creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland calls Transformations an annual student research and creativity conference with presentations and poster sessions.
cards.access_notes: Submission rules and the conference schedule are published for each annual event.

cards.title: Mark Honors Convocation
cards.subtitle: Annual spring academic-recognition ceremony
cards.notes: Check eligibility notices and the ceremony details each spring; the event recognizes top-five-percent students alongside award and scholarship recipients.
cards.short_summary: Cortland’s spring ceremony publicly recognizes academic achievement.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland states that Honors Convocation is held each spring and recognizes students in the top 5% of their class, with awards and scholarships presented.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the annual ceremony’s date, venue and eligibility information.

cards.title: Listen for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Ceremonial university song
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a major ceremony and listen for the song’s closing role at Commencement rather than treating it as background music.
cards.short_summary: The university’s Alma Mater is a continuing part of Cortland’s commencement pageantry.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s commencement tradition page publishes the Alma Mater and identifies it as part of the ceremony’s traditions.
cards.access_notes: The song is associated with formal university ceremonies; event attendance policies apply.

cards.title: Spot the Gonfalons
cards.subtitle: Four banners in the academic procession
cards.notes: At Commencement, look for the university and school banners leading the procession; use the official color guide to identify each gonfalon.
cards.short_summary: Four distinct gonfalons represent the university and its three schools.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says four gonfalons are carried in the academic procession and specifies the university and school color schemes they represent.
cards.access_notes: View them during the formal academic procession at Commencement.

cards.title: Find the Torch of Learning
cards.subtitle: SUNY Cortland’s ceremonial mace
cards.notes: Watch for the silver-and-rosewood mace preceding the platform party at Commencement; it is placed on its stand during official proceedings.
cards.short_summary: The Torch of Learning is Cortland’s named ceremonial mace.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies its mace as the silver-and-rosewood “Torch of Learning,” created by local silversmith John Marshall.
cards.access_notes: This object appears in formal Commencement proceedings; access depends on the ceremony’s event policies.

cards.title: Notice the DiGiusto Medallion
cards.subtitle: President’s Commencement medallion
cards.notes: During Commencement, look for the silver medallion worn by the president and connect its design to the seven valleys of Cortland County.
cards.short_summary: The president’s ceremonial medallion depicts Cortland County’s seven valleys.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland says the DiGiusto Medallion is worn by the president at Commencement and depicts the seven valleys of Cortland County.
cards.access_notes: The medallion is part of the president’s formal Commencement regalia.

boards.school_name: State University of New York at Cortland
boards.title: Your First Weekend at State University of New York at Cortland, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that mixes campus orientation, recreation, arts, food planning and a nearby outdoor walk.

cards.title: Start at Corey Union
cards.subtitle: Campus activities hub
cards.notes: Use the Union as your first indoor landmark, then check the campus calendar or ask about rooms hosting that weekend’s programs.
cards.short_summary: A central point for activities, conferences and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland identifies Corey Union as the center for many university activities and conferences.
cards.access_notes: Check the campus calendar or Campus Activities for event-specific access.

cards.title: Choose a Cortland Nites event
cards.subtitle: Recurring weekend campus programming
cards.notes: Look through the current Cortland Nites listing and select one scheduled event; locations and activities change across the semester.
cards.short_summary: A university-run series of student weekend activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Cortland Nites events are open to all SUNY Cortland students, with scheduled activities at campus and local locations.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current listing for date, location, registration and any event-specific requirements.

cards.title: Find Neubig Hall
cards.subtitle: Dining and campus-store stop
cards.notes: Locate the building early so you know where dining and the College Store are; use the designated east entrance if accessibility is needed.
cards.short_summary: A campus building combining dining, the College Store and auxiliary services.
cards.evidence_claim: Neubig Hall houses the College Store, Neubig Dining and Auxiliary Services Corporation offices.
cards.access_notes: The university identifies the designated accessible entrance on the east side of the building.

cards.title: Get oriented at Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Study spaces and research help
cards.notes: Walk through the main entrance, note the Help Center, and save the floor map before you need a study room or research assistance.
cards.short_summary: A library with study spaces, research help and a café.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Library offers group study rooms, study carrels, the Bookmark Cafe and other spaces.
cards.access_notes: The library’s main entrance leads directly to the Help Center; consult library hours before visiting.

cards.title: See what’s on at Dowd Gallery
cards.subtitle: Dowd Fine Arts Center, Room 106
cards.notes: Check the exhibition page, then visit during posted hours for a quiet art stop; walk-ins are welcome when the university is in session.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery presenting changing exhibitions and public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Dowd Gallery states that all exhibitions and programs are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Walk-ins are welcome; the gallery is closed when the university is not in session. Check posted exhibition hours.

cards.title: Tour the Student Life Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation building
cards.notes: Walk through the recreation hub and identify the pool, track, gym and fitness areas so you can return for an activity that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose recreation facility with fitness and social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland lists a pool, gymnasium, running track, weight room, fitness room and other facilities in the Student Life Center.
cards.access_notes: Fall 2026 main-facility hours are listed as 6 a.m.–midnight weekdays and 8 a.m.–midnight weekends; hours may change during breaks.

cards.title: Try the Climbing Wall orientation
cards.subtitle: Student Life Center climbing gym
cards.notes: Stop in for the required orientation before climbing, and check staffing if you are visiting during a break or near closing time.
cards.short_summary: A climbing gym with roped routes, an auto belay and bouldering.
cards.evidence_claim: The SUNY Cortland climbing gym has a 42-foot roped area, auto belay system and 13-foot bouldering wall.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Sunday–Thursday 3–9 p.m. and Friday–Saturday 3–8 p.m.; call ahead during breaks because staffing is limited.

cards.title: Walk by Red Field
cards.subtitle: SUNY Cortland Stadium Complex
cards.notes: Take a daylight pass through the Stadium Complex and check the athletics schedule for a game or public event before planning to enter seating areas.
cards.short_summary: The Stadium Complex’s large multi-purpose field and grandstand.
cards.evidence_claim: Red Field is a multi-purpose field with a 5,000-seat main grandstand and 1,500 visitor-side seats.
cards.access_notes: Event and spectator access varies; check the athletics or campus event schedule before attending.

cards.title: Plan an Outdoor Pursuits activity
cards.subtitle: Student Life Center outdoor recreation program
cards.notes: Visit the program page to compare climbing, bike, trip and rental options, then follow its current registration or equipment procedures.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation programming for outdoor activity and equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: SUNY Cortland’s Outdoor Pursuits program includes a climbing wall, bike project, equipment rentals and trips.
cards.access_notes: Availability, registration and rental conditions vary by activity; verify details with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Take a daylight trail walk
cards.subtitle: Lime Hollow Nature Center, Cortland
cards.notes: Pick a marked trailhead, bring water, remain on established paths and finish before dusk; review current closures and tick guidance first.
cards.short_summary: A nearby network of public nature trails and trailheads.
cards.evidence_claim: Lime Hollow offers more than 13 miles of open-to-the-public, entrance-fee-free trails that are open dawn to dusk daily.
cards.access_notes: Trails are open dawn to dusk daily. Review trail notices, stay on established trails and follow tick-safety guidance.
